additional_info.subject: RE: 0428311 - ID0428311-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313057100005] upgrade to V7.0.5 - [C1] CRM:00312000100
additional_info.body:
Hello Ferdinand,
I am sorry to hear that an unplanned update to FW v7.0.5 happened on the charger, but I am glad to hear that with the FileHandlerHotfix the communication seems to work fine.
The FileHandlerHotfix is a Hotfix included in v8.0.5, with the scope to avoid excessive log throttling and possible FW corruption, which were caused by an abnormal corruption of a JSON file within sicharge-cp-backend container.
This issue was identified during the month of July, and R&D performed a mass rollout of this Hotfix on the month of August on all chargers that were on v7.0.5. This rollout massive rollout was communicated during several regular touchpoint meetings, but it had no effect on the operation of the chargers.
The Hotfix is now included in v8.0.5, but now that I take a deeper look at the Release Notes, it is not clear that it is included.
As I mentioned in my previous email, I will ask R&D colleague to have a look at the files provided by you, as he is back in office, and I will report that now the charger seems to be updated fine. If this specific Hotfix had an effect to mitigate this issue, I cannot say. I will ask for explanation and will report it to you asap.
Thank you very much for the interesting feedback! I will get back to you with further information and updates from R&D.
With kind regards,

additional_info.body:
Hello Michele,
Hope you're doing well.
This is relating to our discussion on a separate email chain for the inability to access SCB for chargers that are upgraded from version 6.0.3 onwards.
What is common with all these is the inability to connect to AWS IoT.
sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/0938812aa1ee[836]: SiCharge-Configuration error. Could not connect to AWS IoT ablog0tk36tsd-ats.iot.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com    1757556230625
After version 6.0.3, did R&D make a change with how AWS IoT service is accessed?
Specifically around using cross-regional access., or localised redirection?
I ask, because the AWS IoT service is not available in Australia (Melbourne) or New Zealand.
Yet appears to be available in regions, such as Malaysia, Singapore and of course EU-Central (Frankfurt).
You can check which regions have these services here:
AWS Services by Region
I can see it as a very smart move to use the local AWS services for improved speed.
Is there a way we can test this out? E.g. enable a VPN service on the Routers (XF3)?
Either doing this on their own charger to point to New Zealand, or allowing us to make the change locally (providing this doesn't violate any cybersecurity topics).

This is relating to our discussion on a separate email chain for the inability to access SCB for chargers that are upgraded from version 6.0.3 onwards.
What is common with all these is the inability to connect to AWS IoT.
sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/0938812aa1ee[836]: SiCharge-Configuration error. Could not connect to AWS IoT ablog0tk36tsd-ats.iot.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com    1757556230625

Specifically around using cross-regional access., or localised redirection?
I ask, because the AWS IoT service is not available in Australia (Melbourne) or New Zealand.
Yet appears to be available in regions, such as Malaysia, Singapore and of course EU-Central (Frankfurt).
You can check which regions have these services here:
AWS Services by Region
I can see it as a very smart move to use the local AWS services for improved speed.
Is there a way we can test this out? E.g. enable a VPN service on the Routers (XF3)?
Either doing this on their own charger to point to New Zealand, or allowing us to make the change locally (providing this doesn't violate any cybersecurity topics).

additional_info.subject: Status update - Escalation
additional_info.body:
Investigation Status & Ownership:
This case is under investigation by our dedicated R&D team. All details, findings, and ongoing actions are thoroughly documented under
ticket EMOB-20853.
Our R&D team is currently analysing the collected data, including router configurations and system logs, to identify the fundamental root cause.
The
Firmware Product Owner
has been made aware of the severity and urgency of this issue, is included in the CC of this email, and has committed to supporting the investigation to expedite a resolution.
We are prioritizing this to restore reliable operation for our fleet and minimize customer impact.

additional_info.subject: Status update - Feedback from R&D
additional_info.body:
Our team together with R&D has been actively investigating and addressing connectivity issues with the impacted chargers, particularly those running Firmware 7, when connecting to AWS IoT Core. The core challenge identified is high latency impacting reliable communication.
Key Findings & Troubleshooting:
Latency Sensitivity
: R&D team has determined that a latency exceeding +325 ms is problematic for AWS IoT Core (our MQTT service connecting chargers to SCB). Notably, Firmware 7 appears to be more sensitive to this latency compared to Firmware 6.
Testing Environment
: R&D team has successfully deployed a separate SSH tunnel on a charger in the YHI warehouse for testing purposes.
AWS Region Impact:
Initial tests showed high latency.
Creating an AWS IoT Core endpoint in Sydney significantly reduced latency to approximately ~25 ms, which worked successfully with our test client.
AWS Support & Alternatives:
An AWS support ticket was opened to explore solutions.
AWS Global Accelerator was initially suggested, but it's deemed too complex for the given scopes.
Current Approach & Next Steps:
Lightweight PoC (Proof of Concept): R&D team is moving forward with a more lightweight solution to address the latency.
Solution Rollout: If this PoC is successful, we will have a viable solution ready for broader deployment.
Latest Development & Status:
SDK Re-implementation: After exploring and finding AWS infrastructure-side solutions too complex, R&D team opted to re-implement the aws-iot-device-sdk. This re-implementation is currently functional but requires further refinement.
Firmware 7.0.5 Backport: R&D team is working on creating a production-ready backport for Firmware v7.0.5. The current fix is working locally (R&D test machine), and we might anticipate a proper release (either as a hotfix or a new v7 version) within a few days. This will also pave the way for a v8 release.
Dependency Resolution: We are addressing some dependency issues related to building the older v7 version, which are expected to be resolved very soon.
Future Alignment: Once a production-ready artifact is available, R&D teams will coordinate internally to plan the subsequent steps. These will be communicated to Service teams accordingly
